Coach Curt Cignetti led his Indiana Hoosiers to a 27-13 home win over USC football that included a hilarious situation involving kicker Caden Chittenden . Cignetti made a tough decision before the game that cleared the way for Grant Wilson to start, an opportunity the 25-year-old starter made the most of in Bloomington, Indiana. Wilson had 305 yards passing with two touchdowns and one interception, continuing Cignetti’s tradition of getting the most out of new players in big games. He had a refreshing message for new backup and teammate Josh Hoover after the huge home win, as shared by reporter Matt Fortuna. “It’s awesome, this brotherhood that we have right here, it’s second to none…These guys have been nothing but great mentors to me, Fernando (Mendoza) last year, Josh (Hoover) this year, I just want to give a shoutout to Josh, he’s been through so much with his shoulder, he’s worked so hard to come back, this is still his team,” Wilson said after his Hoosiers pounded Lincoln Riley’s Trojans at Memorial Stadium. Wilson did a better job of taking care of the football with 305 yards passing and two touchdowns, along with one interception. The IU offensive line lived up to Wilson’s lofty billing as Khobie Wilson ran for over 80 yards and a score. In the passing game, Nick Marsh had 80 receiving yards on four catches as Wilson’s favorite target. At 9-1, IU looks like a smart bet for a College Football Playoff spot. top.title: UFC 334 video: Stephen ‘Wonderboy’ Thompson retires with spinning wheel kick knockout over Charles Radtke
top.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson ended his career in style with a spectacular spinning back kick knockout over Charles Radtke to cap off the UFC 334 prelims. After already announcing that Saturday would serve as his retirement fight, Thompson delivered another classic finish after he uncorked the kick and sent Radtke crashing to the canvas. The end officially came at 2:54 in the third round with Thompson celebrating his win by laying down his gloves in the octagon for the last time. WONDERBOY WINS BY WHEEL KICK KO WHAT AN ENDING TO HIS UFC CAREER 👏 [ #UFC334 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/WfTOJTvDcP — UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) November 15, 2026 “I’ve been with the UFC for almost 15 years, I couldn’t have asked for better than a spin back kick to the dome,” Thompson said after his win. “I don’t care if your hands are up, a spin back kick, you’re going down. I told myself I wasn’t going to cry. I just want to say I love you.” Radtke was on the gas pedal from the jump before diving for a takedown before the first minute expired. Thompson was quick to start working his way up with Radtke doing his best to maintain his position on top. Thompson eventually worked his way back up with Radtke holding onto the clinch against the cage. When he finally broke free, Thompson started to establish his jab while keeping Radtke at a distance while playing counter fighter from the outside. In the second round, Thompson kept chipping away from the outside with Radtke still trying to pressure forward. Radtke eventually shot in for the takedown but Thompson resisted effectively. Thompson then started getting a little looser with his striking, tossing out straight punches and then mixing in a variety of kicks. Thompson continued pouring it on with Radtke nearly wilting with time running out in the round. With five minutes remaining, Thompson was quick to establish his striking again including a heel kick to the face. Radtke was clearly slowing down and Thompson was taking full advantage. Thompson kept tossing out combinations and Radtke was struggling to answer with his own offense. Thompson then unleashed a spinning back kick that blasted Radtke and sent him to the canvas for the final time. Thompson ends his career as one of the most lethal strikers in UFC history and a top welterweight for almost his entire time in the promotion. He walks away with another highlight reel knockout to go out on a victory.

Those minutes just aren’t there right now for the big club. With the Coachella Valley Lakers, Mañon is able to expand his skill set such as playing point guard . Another aspect of Mañon’s game that he can attack in the G League is his rebounding. top.title: MSU football fumbles away another win in 21-14 loss to Washington
top.description: EAST LANSING − Michigan State football could not finish the job. The Spartans were forced to play backup QB Cam Fancher after a second-quarter left hand/arm injury to starter Alessio Milivojevic, but they could not make enough plays on offense in a 21-14 loss to Washington on Saturday, Nov. 14, at chilly Spartan Stadium. MSU (3-7, 1-6 Big Ten ) is now set to miss a bowl game for a fifth consecutive season, while the Huskies (6-4, 3-4) are now bowl eligible. UW landed in the East Lansing area at 3 a.m. after the flight outage nationwide Friday afternoon. MSU's Liam Boyd missed a go-ahead 50-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter after the offense gained just 1 yard following a UW muffed punt. Fancher flipped an awful INT late in the third quarter in the red zone, trying to do too much while in the grasp of a defender. Demond Williams Jr. connected with standout sophomore receiver Chris Lawson for two touchdowns in the first half and two key third-down conversions on the winning drive, finished by Jayden Limar's 1-yard run with 2:24 left in the game. Fancher and MSU kept the game alive with two fourth-down conversions, but lost a fumble in UW territory to end the game. This story will be updated. top.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 42 - Ed Ratleff
top.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the second of 12 who wore the No. 42, Ed Ratleff. After ending his college career at Cal State Long Beach, he was picked up with the sixth overall selection of the 1973 NBA Draft by the Houston Rockets. The Bellefontaine, Ohio native played all 5 seasons of his pro career with Houston, leaving the league as a player afterward. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Ratleff wore only jersey No. 42 and put up 8.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 1.3 steals per game. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Sean Higgins. An alum of Michigan, he was picked up with the 54th overall selection of the 1990 NBA Draft by the San Antonio Spurs. The Los Angeles, California native played the first 2 seasons of his pro career with the Spurs. He also played for the Orlando Magic and Golden State Warriors before he signed with the (then) New Jersey (now, Brooklyn) Nets in 1994. His stay with the team lasted until he was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in 1995. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Higgins put up 4.7 points and 1.4 rebounds per game. top.title: Sympathy for Thomas Tuchel?
top.description: (Photo by John Walton - Pool/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former England manager Roy Hodgson has expressed his sympathy for football managers who find themselves under intense scrutiny, pointing out how easy it is for people outside the game to criticize decisions without understanding the pressures involved. Hodgson, who could be a little biased on the topic give his long track record of being a head coach, reflected on the familiar divide between those making decisions on the touchline and those watching comfortably from the stands or their sofas. “Oh, absolutely. Absolutely sympathizing, because in all these situations you’re back to the famous ‘man in the arena’ story, or whatever it was. It’s all about the man in the arena. And we who aren’t in the arena are in a comfortable position. We just have to sit back and say, ‘I wouldn’t have done it that way myself.’ So of course, I’m very sympathetic about that,” Hodgson told The Jeff Stelling Show, produced by OLBG . The former manager also highlighted how football is often judged far too simplistically, with the final score oversh adowing everything that happens throughout a match. “Games are judged at the end, by the result. An awful lot goes on between the first minute and the 95th or 98th, or whatever it is now,” said Hodgson. “An awful lot goes on which has an enormous effect upon the game, but it will be glossed over, in a way. And when the final result comes in, that’s when people will decide, ‘Ah, this is where we got it wrong.’” It is a reminder that managing a football club is rarely as straightforward as it appears from the outside. Decisions are made under enormou s pressure, circumstances change throughout matches, and sometimes the result dictates the narrative regardless of everything that came before it. Hodgson knows better than most that be ing the person in the arena is a very different experience from being an armchair critic. Join the conversation! top.description: Los Angeles Dodgers legend Orel Hershiser sat down with Dodgers Nation to talk about how the organization responds to its disappointing loss. What Hershiser sees from the Dodgers organization The Dodgers, as everyone knows, were bounced out after getting punched square in the teeth by a Milwaukee Brewers team that acted like a buzzsaw. To varying degrees, the Dodgers have always punched back during their current dynasty, putting up a fight in every series. nigeria.description: By Olaosebikan Olaniyi Marriage is a contract, and every serious contract should be explicit about its most important terms. Sex is central to marriage. It affects emotional bonding, physical health, fidelity, and long-term satisfaction. Leaving it to assumptions and unspoken expectations is why so many marriages fail. A sex agreement as part of the marriage contract makes sense for three clear reasons. 1. It Creates Clarity and Honesty Most couples never have an honest conversation about their sexual needs, boundaries, frequency, and values before marriage. They assume love will handle it. A formal agreement forces that conversation. It allows both partners to state what they want, what they do not want, and what is non-negotiable. Clarity before marriage prevents resentment after marriage. 2. It Protects Consent and Mutual Respect Marriage does not equal automatic consent. A sex agreement affirms that both partners have ongoing rights over their own bodies. It can define consent, right to say no without punishment, agreement on fidelity, protection, and respect for periods of illness, pregnancy, stress, or trauma. This protects both husband and wife and builds a culture of respect, not entitlement. 3. It Prevents Future Conflict Many divorces and infidelity cases stem from sexual incompatibility and unmet expectations. One partner wants sex daily, the other weekly. One sees pornography or open marriage as acceptable, the other does not. One wants children immediately, the other wants to delay. If these issues were agreed upon in writing as part of the marriage contract, couples would either resolve them early or realize they are not compatible before making a lifelong commitment. Including a sex agreement does not make marriage less romantic. It makes it more mature. We sign agreements for money, property, and children. Why should we ignore the very act that creates children and sustains intimacy? Marriage should include a clear, mutual, and voluntary agreement about sex. nigeria.title: Hidden Curriculum of Leadership: What does the environment teach leaders?
nigeria.description: By Dayo Oyinlola Institutions are ecosystems made up of individual units that live in symbiotic relationships with each other. In these environments, information is processed dynamically and learning occurs both formally and informally. We must consider this reality when discussing leadership development. Leaders learn through written documents and institutional codes of conduct: values, laws, behavioral manuals, KPIs and OKRs that organisations establish to hold leaders accountable. And then there are the experiences nobody formally teaches, but everyone learns. A young executive watches how decisions are made. They notice who gets rewarded and who gets overlooked. They observe what happens when someone challenges authority, misses a target, refuses to compromise or asks an uncomfortable question. Nobody necessarily sits them down to teach these lessons. We often think of leadership development as something that happens through formal training, coaching, mentoring and experience. All of these matters, but leaders are also continuously shaped by the systems, institutions, cultures and circumstances within which they operate. And sometimes, the lessons being taught by the environment are very different from the lesson’s organisations believe they are teaching. Consider an organisation that claims to encourage employees to challenge ideas, yet senior leaders consistently dismiss people who disagree with them. Employees then learn that deference is safer than speaking up. Over time, people respond to what they experience rather than what they are told. The environment teaches what is rewarded. It teaches what is tolerated. It teaches how power works, whose voice matters and whether speaking up is valued or punished. It teaches people what leadership really means when it is exercised, not what the organisation says leadership means. This becomes particularly important in difficult operating environments. But there is another question worth asking: What happens when the environment consistently makes the wrong behaviour easier than the right one? If people repeatedly experience an environment where ethical behaviour is punished and unethical behaviour is rewarded, the environment itself becomes part of their leadership development. This is why integrity cannot survive indefinitely as an individual act of courage. For it to become sustainable, it must become part of the collective environment. nigeria.title: I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu
nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Obioma Ofoegbu has spoken about the challenges of being stereotyped because of her plus-size physique, saying she is determined to establish herself as a versatile performer capable of taking on diverse roles. In an interview with Potpourri, Ofoegbu said she had repeatedly been offered roles that portrayed her as an older woman or confined her to characters typically associated with plus-size actresses. “My biggest challenge when I started was not being stereotyped because of my body type. A lot of times, they tried to give me roles just because I’m a plus-size woman. They would make me older in some movies or give me the same stories that a plus-size woman is expected to tell,” she said. The actress, who officially began her film career in 2020 after years of participating in stage plays and theatre productions during her school days, said she had rejected several roles in a bid to break away from such limitations. “I’m young. I don’t have to play an older woman or a married woman just because I’m plus-size. I don’t want to be placed in a box because of my looks, my appearance, or where I live,” she added. Speaking about her most challenging role, Ofoegbu identified her performance in Africa Magic’s series, The Low Priest, where she portrayed a villainous character who undergoes a transformation. She described the experience as physically demanding, revealing that she had to learn more Igbo, chant incantations and endure challenging filming conditions. The experience, she said, strengthened her confidence in her abilities and taught her that preparation and resilience could help her handle demanding characters. Despite her preference for diverse roles, Ofoegbu admitted that economic realities in Nigeria could make accepting stereotypical roles necessary, particularly for emerging actors trying to establish themselves financially. “I’m not a Funke Akindele yet. I’m not big enough to be producing as I please, so definitely I would take up those roles. I would grow as an actor, save, build and get my face out there,” she said. She also described acting as an uncertain source of income for emerging performers, advising actors to develop alternative income streams rather than depend entirely on film roles. On film promotion, the actress, who also has experience as an executive producer, maintained that actors should support projects they feature in but insisted that producers must have independent marketing strategies. Her long-term ambition, she said, is to have her work recognised beyond Africa and collaborate with filmmakers across different parts of the world. “I’m an actor, I’m not just a Nollywood actor. nigeria.title: Nigeria needs 700,000 housing units annually to tackle deficit, Durojaye says
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Chairman of the Board of Directors of Gateway Mortgage Bank Limited, Samuel Durojaye, has said that Nigeria needs to construct approximately 700,000 housing units annually over the next decade to significantly reduce its housing deficit. Durojaye noted that achieving the target would require sustained investment, improved access to housing finance and greater collaboration among key stakeholders in the real estate and mortgage sectors. Durojaye, who disclosed this at the 9th Annual General Meeting of Gateway Mortgage Bank Limited, held in Abeokuta, Ogun State described mortgage institutions as vital to bridging the country’s housing gap, explaining that they play a dual role in facilitating homeownership for individuals and providing property developers with access to the financing needed to expand housing construction. He stressed that strengthening mortgage financing would improve the capacity of developers to deliver more housing units and make homeownership more accessible to Nigerians. He added that increasing the supply of affordable housing would help ease pressure on the property market, particularly by moderating the persistent rise in rental costs across major urban centres. According to him, addressing the housing deficit requires a sustained focus on expanding housing supply and improving access to affordable financing to ensure that more Nigerians can secure decent and affordable homes. The chairman, however, identified access to long-term funding as one of the major constraints confronting mortgage banks, explaining that the long repayment periods associated with housing loans made it difficult for institutions to rely on short-term deposits. “The minimum tenure for a mortgage is 10, 15 or 20 years. You cannot take people’s money when they expect it back in 90 days and put it into a property that will not pay back until 15 years,” he said. He therefore called for funding arrangements that would align with the long-term nature of mortgage financing, stressing that sustainable access to capital was essential for expanding homeownership. Durojaye also urged Nigerians, particularly young professionals and salary earners, to embrace mortgage financing early in their careers, rather than commit substantial portions of their income to recurring rent payments. “Instead of paying ₦2m in rent every year, why don’t you buy a house and start paying ₦200,000 monthly from your salary?” he asked. He explained that mortgage arrangements enabled prospective homeowners to spread the cost of acquiring properties over an agreed period, allowing them to build long-term assets instead of continually spending on rent. nigeria.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
nigeria.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. nigeria.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
nigeria.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. entertainment.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. Thompson continued pouring it on with Radtke nearly wilting with time running out in the round. With five minutes remaining, Thompson was quick to establish his striking again including a heel kick to the face. Radtke was clearly slowing down and Thompson was taking full advantage. Thompson kept tossing out combinations and Radtke was struggling to answer with his own offense. Thompson then unleashed a spinning back kick that blasted Radtke and sent him to the canvas for the final time. Thompson ends his career as one of the most lethal strikers in UFC history and a top welterweight for almost his entire time in the promotion. sports.title: Sympathy for Thomas Tuchel?
sports.description: (Photo by John Walton - Pool/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former England manager Roy Hodgson has expressed his sympathy for football managers who find themselves under intense scrutiny, pointing out how easy it is for people outside the game to criticize decisions without understanding the pressures involved. Hodgson, who could be a little biased on the topic give his long track record of being a head coach, reflected on the familiar divide between those making decisions on the touchline and those watching comfortably from the stands or their sofas. “Oh, absolutely. Absolutely sympathizing, because in all these situations you’re back to the famous ‘man in the arena’ story, or whatever it was. It’s all about the man in the arena. And we who aren’t in the arena are in a comfortable position. We just have to sit back and say, ‘I wouldn’t have done it that way myself.’ So of course, I’m very sympathetic about that,” Hodgson told The Jeff Stelling Show, produced by OLBG . The former manager also highlighted how football is often judged far too simplistically, with the final score oversh adowing everything that happens throughout a match. “Games are judged at the end, by the result. An awful lot goes on between the first minute and the 95th or 98th, or whatever it is now,” said Hodgson. “An awful lot goes on which has an enormous effect upon the game, but it will be glossed over, in a way. And when the final result comes in, that’s when people will decide, ‘Ah, this is where we got it wrong.’” It is a reminder that managing a football club is rarely as straightforward as it appears from the outside. Decisions are made under enormou s pressure, circumstances change throughout matches, and sometimes the result dictates the narrative regardless of everything that came before it. technology.description: STARBASE, Texas —The black and silver ship fell out of the sky, emerging from the cloud deck near the very end of its flight. Incongruously, the rocket flew horizontal until the last moment when three Raptor rocket engines ignited and it swooped into a vertical position. Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms. Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
science.description: null Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it hit the century mark on Saturday in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron met the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The Electron rocket that flew Rocket Lab's 100th mission sported some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" was Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. And all went to plan on the mission: Electron's upper "kick stage" deployed a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths. science.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
science.description: null LOS ANGELES — The California Science Center officially opened its brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public today (Nov. 13). After more than three decades in development, folks can finally visit the Los Angeles science museum's massive new wing. For most of us, the biggest draw is its centerpiece: the retired space shuttle Endeavour , sitting upright in launch position, towering at nearly 200 feet (61 meters) tall. "It just takes your breath away when you see that reveal and the doors open and you get to look at it for the first time. It's just — it's overwhelming," former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman told Space.com during a visit to the museum. Reisman flew on two space shuttle missions during his astronaut career, the first of which was on Endeavour. The space shuttle Endeavour. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) "There are people that come from all over the world, and when they come to Los Angeles, they're going to have the opportunity to see it, too," Reisman added. "The exposure it's going to have is just a force multiplier. There are so many people that can have that opportunity to bring their kids here and show them [the shuttle] and have that experience." Entering into this exhibit is an experience in and of itself, as I can personally attest; I was among of group of reporters who got a sneak peek at the new wing on Oct. 28. A video presentation ends in a dramatic reveal: Visitors walk into a space where the enormous shuttle, which flew 25 missions to Earth orbit from 1992 to 2011, feels truly larger than life. The new Endeavour exhibit features a replica launch tower, from which you can look down at the shuttle. (Image credit: Future) There are a number of interactive exhibits around the base of Endeavour, which you can slide down to (though, of course, you can also take the elevator or stairs). From a shuttle landing simulator to a replica of a shuttle cockpit that you can sit in, to shuttle tires and space tech from across decades of spaceflight history, there's an incredible variety of space artifacts to both observe and interact with. As for Endeavour itself: It is open, so you can peer inside to see the robotic arm tucked away among a myriad of handles, straps and electronic gear inside. And you can see the shuttle from underneath all the way to the top. A replica of the space shuttle Endeavour's flight deck. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) You can lie on the floor underneath the shuttle's engines, for example, and then take an elevator up the launch tower to come face-to-face with Endeavour's nose. There's even a transparent floor at the top that allows you to stand above the shuttle (though if you have a fear of heights, this might not be for you). science.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
science.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. science.title: 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child
science.description: null "Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving " Event Horizon ", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men. Mars rover, nice. Golden Milestone Studio Spacesuits, check. Golden Milestone Studio Crafting, of course. Golden Milestone Studio OH SWEET JESUS! Get it away, get it away. Golden Milestone Studio OK, we're good. Mining, cool. Golden Milestone Studio Riding a quad bike on Mars, yes please. Golden Milestone Studio Growing potatoes on Mars, just like that guy in the movie. Golden Milestone Studio Opening a box with power tools, seems excessive but sure. Golden Milestone Studio NOPE! Nope, nope, nope, I'm out! Golden Milestone Studio Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars ? I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.
